questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: My main motivation was to experience living abroad, broaden my horizons and meet new people. I especially wanted the social experience of living and studying in another country and the opportunity to form new friendships with people from different backgrounds.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Heidelberg was the only exchange destination available to me in Germany when I applied. I specifically wanted to study in Germany, so I chose Heidelberg. If more German destinations had been available, Munich would probably have been my first choice, but I regret nothing, Heidelberg was very lovely

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would rate my overall experience 9/10, mainly because of the social experience. I met many great people, made close friendships and really enjoyed living abroad. The main downside was the amount of German bureaucracy and administration, which could sometimes be quite frustrating and unnecessarily complicated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of the necessary information was available, although it sometimes took some time to figure out the different administrative procedures and where to find the relevant information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information and guidance from the International Relations Office and the university regarding enrolment, course registration and practical matters. There were also orientation activities for international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student accommodation was available through Studierendenwerk Heidelberg. I lived in a furnished room in a four-person shared apartment (WG) in the student accommodation at Im Neuenheimer Feld.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My shared apartment had a communal kitchen where we could cook our own meals. There were also university canteens (Mensa) where students could buy affordable meals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend student housing, especially as an exchange student. It was affordable and a good way to meet other students. I lived in Im Neuenheimer Feld, which is mainly the natural sciences campus. Since most of my courses were located there, I was lucky to live very close to where I studied. It is a bit outside the city centre, but still well connected. The accommodation is fairly basic, but it has everything you need. I would recommend applying for housing as early as possible, as getting a room is not guaranteed.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration was mainly done through heiCO, Heidelberg University's online system. After enrolment and receiving my university account, I could search for courses and register online. Some courses had different registration procedures or deadlines, so it was important to check the information for each individual course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information was available through heiCO and the university websites, and the International Relations Office and departmental coordinators could help with questions. Lecturers were also helpful when there were questions about specific courses or exams.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for the courses I wanted without any major problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the course catalogue and registration deadlines early, as the registration process can vary between courses. I would also recommend having some backup courses in mind, since the final course catalogue may not be available until relatively close to the start of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic experience was mixed. Some courses were very interesting and well taught, while others were less organized than I expected. The course and exam structure also varied considerably between courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My courses were at master's level because most of the English-taught courses relevant to me were offered at that level. Overall, I found the academic level comparable to UCPH, although the difficulty varied quite a lot between courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was basically the same as at UCPH, although I found it more difficult to get professors to respond to emails.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Computational Macroeconomics. It was relatively easy and had a very manageable workload for an 8 ECTS course, making it a good choice for exchange students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any major unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Student housing was cheaper than I expected, and groceries were generally reasonably priced. Beer in bars was also quite cheap compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Never used it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were university sports, student organisations and various events for international and exchange students. I did not personally make much use of these, as most of my social life came from friends I met through Erasmus events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend joining the events for international and exchange students, especially at the beginning of the semester. It is a great way to meet people and build a social circle early on.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get the Deutschlandticket and use it to explore Germany. Frankfurt, Freiburg and Stuttgart are easy trips from Heidelberg, and cities such as Munich are also worth visiting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. German culture is quite similar to Danish culture, so I did not experience any major difficulties adjusting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really. Most of my friends were other international and exchange students, but the local students were generally very friendly and interested in getting to know exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was the amount of bureaucracy and paperwork in Germany. Many administrative processes felt more complicated and less digital than I was used to in Denmark. Also, basically all bars closed around 1 AM, which was quite annoying if you wanted a proper night out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: German beer, german football, Frühlingsfest

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for student housing as early as possible.

Make an effort to meet other exchange students from the beginning – the social part was by far the best part of my exchange.

Get the Deutschlandticket and use the opportunity to travel around Germany.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for quite a lot of bureaucracy and paperwork, especially at the beginning and end of your stay. Apart from that, Heidelberg is a very easy and enjoyable city to live in as an exchange student.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely the people I met. I made close friends from many different countries, and the social experience was by far the most rewarding part of my exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The German bureaucracy was probably the biggest challenge. Also, coming from Copenhagen, I found it quite strange that most nightlife in Heidelberg ends around 1 AM.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall, I had a great exchange experience and would definitely recommend Heidelberg to other exchange students, especially for the social experience. The people I met and the friendships I made were by far the highlight of my semester.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
